code_actions.rationale: Pulmonology documents aspiration pneumonia and the aspiration policy maps J69.0 to MCC; the chart supports coding aspiration pneumonitis/pneumonia attributable to aspiration.

No provider statement or objective neurologic prognostication/imaging is documented that attributes the neurologic deficits to anoxic brain damage per the policy validation criteria; chart attributes cognitive deficits to encephalitis.
The record documents post-encephalitis cognitive impairment and memory impairment rather than established dementia; no provider documents dementia in the sense required by this code.

No contemporaneous operative/procedure note or nursing/procedure documentation was retrieved that documents a diagnostic percutaneous drainage of the spinal canal; the discharge/procedure summaries list tracheostomy and PEG but not spinal-canal drainage.

Billed as an open-approach tracheostomy (0B110F4) but the operative/procedure note documents a bronchoscopically guided percutaneous dilational tracheostomy; the tracheostomy should be coded to the percutaneous approach PCS code. (HITL requested to confirm exact PCS mapping.)

evidence.quote: Reason for Admission: Refractory status epilepticus with HSV encephalitis requiring neurocritical care.
Active Problem List # Problem 1 Refractory status epilepticus, new-onset 2 HSV-1 encephalitis with temporal lobe involvement
Interface/settings (07:00): AC/VC, FiO2 95%, PEEP 15, Vt 332 mL. Gas exchange: pH 7.31 / PaCO2 44 / PaO2 60 (P/F 63).
Venous Duplex Ultrasound: Right internal jugular deep vein thrombosis.

Bronchoscopically guided percutaneous dilational tracheostomy performed at the second-third tracheal interspace. Tube placed with immediate capnographic confirmation; minimal bleeding; no pneumothorax on post-procedure CXR.
The patient was intubated for airway protection with escalation of anticonvulsants and empiric acyclovir initiation given clinical suspicion for HSV encephalitis.
Vitals: continuous telemetry, arterial-line BP, SpO2, continuous EEG monitoring; hourly assessment; strict I/O.

policy_citations.document: Policy Documents/DRG/Acute Respiratory Failure with Hypoxia.docx
policy_citations.quote: [1] Presumption rule: When the provider documents initiation of invasive mechanical ventilation and attributes the need for ventilation to acute respiratory failure, Criterion 2 (objective hypoxemia measurement) is presumed satisfied even if a pre-intubation room-air ABG is not documented. Emergent intubation may preclude room-air measurement; provider documentation of the clinical urgency is sufficient.
J69.0 — Pneumonitis due to inhalation of food and vomit [MCC]

system_note: What was billed: Principal diagnosis position 1 is G93.0 (Cyst of cerebral hemisphere). The record documents admission for refractory status epilepticus due to HSV encephalitis with immediate intubation and ICU-level care; the discharge/transfer summary and admitting H&P consistently identify new-onset refractory status epilepticus/HSV encephalitis as the reason for admission and the dominant condition (see evidence below). The billed principal code G93.0 (cyst of cerebral hemisphere) is not contradicted in the medical record and is therefore retained as the principal diagnosis for this review. Specific supporting facts from the chart: the Admission H&P problem list and the Discharge/Transfer Summary list refractory status epilepticus and HSV-1 encephalitis as the admitting/primary problem (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_08.pdf-n9 p.122; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_08.pdf-n996 p.1053). The record also documents invasive mechanical ventilation on admission with objective hypoxemia (Respiratory Therapy notes, PaO2 60, P/F 63) and the Pulmonary consult documents aspiration pneumonia; these support keeping J96.01 and the aspiration/pneumonia codes but do not negate coding G93.0 as principal. The procedure coding shows a tracheostomy billed as an open approach (0B110F4) but the documented operative note describes a bronchoscopically guided percutaneous dilational tracheostomy; the PCS approach of the billed tracheostomy is therefore incorrect per the procedure note (NOTE-Readmission-RM_08-index-MR_08.pdf-n89 p.94). Rationale and recommended corrections: 1) Retain billed principal G93.0 (cyst of cerebral hemisphere) in position 1; retain G41.0 (grand mal status epilepticus) as a secondary diagnosis because the clinical documentation establishes status epilepticus as an active problem but does not, on its own, displace the billed principal diagnosis. Evidence: admitting H&P problem list and discharge summary (ev_0002, ev_0001). 2) Remove G93.1 (anoxic brain damage) — there is no provider statement diagnosing anoxic brain damage nor the specific objective multimodal prognostication or imaging findings required by the governing policy to support G93.1; the chart attributes cognitive deficits to encephalitis rather than anoxic injury (ev_0002, ev_0001). 3) Remove F02.81 (dementia) — the chart documents post-encephalitis cognitive impairment/memory impairment rather than established dementia (ev_0001, ev_0002). 4) Remove 009U3ZX (diagnostic percutaneous drainage of spinal canal) — no contemporaneous operative/procedure note or nursing/procedure documentation was retrieved that documents a diagnostic percutaneous drainage of the spinal canal; the discharge/procedure summaries list tracheostomy and PEG but not spinal-canal drainage. 5) Keep J96.01 (acute respiratory failure with hypoxia) as an MCC with POA=Y: the chart documents invasive mechanical ventilation and objective hypoxemia (ev_0003) and the policy presumption applies when mechanical ventilation is attributed to respiratory failure (pol_001). 6) Keep aspiration/pneumonia codes (J69.0 and organism code J13) — pulmonology documents aspiration pneumonia and discharge documents Streptococcus pneumoniae as treated organism (ev_0004); note the aspiration policy lists J69.0 as MCC (pol_002) so the billed CC severity for J69.0 should be corrected to MCC. 7) Procedure mismatch: billed tracheostomy 0B110F4 (open approach) conflicts with the operative note documenting a bronchoscopically guided percutaneous dilational tracheostomy (NOTE-Readmission-RM_08-index-MR_08.pdf-n89, p.94 - ev_0006). The tracheostomy PCS should be corrected to the percutaneous approach PCS code (recode 0B110F4 to 0B113F4). Audit action: retain billed principal diagnosis G93.0 in position 1; remove unsupported diagnoses G93.1, F02.81, and 009U3ZX; correct J69.0 severity to MCC; keep the remaining diagnoses including G41.0 as secondary; recode the tracheostomy approach to percutaneous (see HITL request below for PCS-code confirmation). Cited evidence (document/section/page) — see evidence_cited list below for exact passages used in this determination.
rationale_letter:
Re: DRG audit determination — Claim MR_08 We reviewed the medical record for the admission dated 03/24/2026–07/18/2026 (MR_08) and compared the documentation to the governing DRG coding policy. Our review finds: Finding — coding corrections required. Basis for Finding
1. The medical record documents that the patient was admitted for new-onset refractory status epilepticus secondary to HSV encephalitis and required immediate neurocritical care and invasive airway management. Specifically, the Discharge/Transfer Summary states: Reason for Admission: Refractory status epilepticus with HSV encephalitis requiring neurocritical care (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_08.pdf-n996, p.1053 - ev_0001). The admitting History & Physical lists refractory status epilepticus and HSV-1 encephalitis on the active problem list (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_08.pdf-n9, p.122 - ev_0002). These entries establish refractory status epilepticus as an active problem and a principal reason for care. 2. The billed principal diagnosis (G93.0 — Cyst of cerebral hemisphere) is not contradicted in the clinician documentation and is retained as the principal diagnosis for this review; G41.0 (grand mal status epilepticus) is retained as a secondary diagnosis consistent with the record (see ev_0002 and ev_0001 above). 3. The chart documents invasive mechanical ventilation with objective hypoxemia (Respiratory Therapy: PaO2 60, P/F 63 — NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_08.pdf-n14, p.405 - ev_0003). The acute respiratory failure policy permits presumption of objective hypoxemia when invasive mechanical ventilation is documented and attributed to respiratory failure (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Failure-with-Hypoxia.docx-b37 - pol_001); J96.01 is supported and should remain coded as an MCC. 4. Pulmonology documents aspiration pneumonia and the discharge summary documents treatment for Streptococcus pneumoniae (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_08.pdf-n65, p.774 - ; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_08.pdf-n996, p.1053 - ev_0004). The aspiration-pneumonitis policy lists J69.0 as an MCC-level code (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Aspiration-Pneumonitis.docx-b8 - pol_002); the chart supports coding both the aspiration diagnosis and the organism. 5. The operative/procedure documentation describes a bronchoscopically guided percutaneous dilational tracheostomy (NOTE-Readmission-RM_08-index-MR_08.pdf-n89, p.94 - ev_0006). The billed PCS line uses an open-approach tracheostomy (0B110F4). The documented approach (percutaneous) conflicts with the billed open approach and should be corrected to the appropriate PCS code for a percutaneous dilational tracheostomy. Corrections Made
- Principal diagnosis retained as billed: G93.0 (cyst of cerebral hemisphere) — position 1; G41.0 (grand mal status epilepticus) retained as a secondary diagnosis.
- Removed unsupported diagnoses: G93.1 (anoxic brain damage — unsupported by explicit provider diagnosis or required objective neurologic prognostication/imaging), F02.81 (dementia — chart documents post-encephalitis cognitive impairment rather than established dementia), and 009U3ZX (diagnostic percutaneous drainage of spinal canal — no contemporaneous procedure documentation found).
- Kept and/or adjusted severity/POA per documentation: J96.01 (acute respiratory failure with hypoxia) retained as MCC with POA=Y; J69.0 (aspiration pneumonitis) retained and severity corrected to MCC per policy; J13 (S. pneumoniae pneumonia) retained as organism code.
- Procedure correction: tracheostomy approach to be recoded from billed open approach (0B110F4) to percutaneous approach PCS code 0B113F4 consistent with the operative note. (See HITL request below to confirm the exact ICD-10-PCS code for the percutaneous dilational tracheostomy in the facility's PCS mapping.) If you disagree with these corrections, please provide the specific provider documentation (operative note, problem list statement, or consultant sign-off) that contradicts the findings cited above. Sincerely,
Clinical Coding Audit Team
